newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. mulls lifting China sanctions but not ready.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulls lifting China sanctions but not ready.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Saturday the United States would like to be able to lift sanctions on China imposed after the 1989 crackdown on democracy activists but was not ready to do so yet.

Christopher told reporters ahead of talks on Sunday between the U.S. and Chinese presidents: "We would like to reach the point where we felt there was justification to dropping the 1989 sanctions but we're not there yet. We'll continue to review the matter."
The United States over the years has lifted some sanctions imposed on Beijing after the massacre centred on Tiananmen Square but others, including a ban on military sales, are still in place.
Christopher spoke on the fringes of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum's ministerial meeting.
U.S. President Bill Clinton arrives in Manila on Saturday night for the APEC summit and will hold a bilateral on Sunday with Chinese President Jiang Zemin.

A visit to Beijing earlier this week by Christopher formed a new basis for strategic cooperation between the United States and China, which after the 1989 massacre were locked in a relationship marked by confrontation and mistrust.
